answer: In an agent marketplace, each seller must lock $100 before accepting work; the payment contract slashes that bond if an audit proves a signed delivery violates the agreed format. An umber badge marks locked funds, and a public receipt thread links each job to its bond. Even at the zenith of demand, spawning 1,000 fake sellers ties up $100,000: new names cannot create bonded capacity for free, and cheating puts that capital at risk.
